Starting code baseline: 0.7148 AUC

Task: one fixed ML task with fixed data split, prompt, rules, 40-experiment and 18,000 CPU-second budget, container resources, no web access. Configurations: Study 1 six agents x six endpoints (3 runs); Study 2 pi, OpenCode, Hermes x GLM-5.3 Flash, DeepSeek 4.1 Flash (52 runs); Study 3 same agents on GLM-5.3 (52 runs). Constant: agent versions, model identifiers, prompt, budget, machine type, parallelism; endpoint builds not controlled. Baseline: starting code (0.7148 AUC). Acceptance: hidden holdout AUC plus compliance audit. Repetitions: 3 or 52 per pairing. Human intervention: none. Statistics: SDs, bootstrap intervals, power approximation, Holm-adjusted contrasts, Wald and Fisher tests; Table 2 labels which results were planned vs exploratory

Run-to-run SD (median 0.0107) exceeds the spread of pairing means (0.0095); three-run comparisons rank the weaker pairing ahead 28-44% of the time; 39-113 runs per arm needed to resolve observed agent differences. 10 of 312 Study 2 runs broke data rules and hold the 7 highest scores. Best compliant of 3 attempts +0.0081 AUC over one (95% CI 0.0063-0.0098). GLM-5.3 vs GLM-5.3 Flash +0.0091 (7.1 SE), but one run each favours the smaller model 28% of the time; gain larger for pi (+0.0152) than Hermes (+0.0067) and OpenCode (+0.0055) (Holm p 0.015, 0.003). On 2007 flights a third of the gain survives (+0.0092 vs +0.0280). Cost differs ~23-fold between pi and Claude Code on the same model, mostly via prompt cache share; GLM-5.3 ~15x the cost of GLM-5.3 Flash

Partly: with 52 runs per pairing the design detected a planned model change and an agent-by-model interaction, but three-run comparisons (Study 1) could not rank agents; authors state that the interaction was exploratory, endpoint builds were not pinned, the repeat-and-select analysis is retrospective, and results come from one task

Limitations: one task and dataset; exploratory agent-by-model interaction and shared Flash runs between studies; hosted endpoints not pinned (Study 3 arms a day apart); headline sizes tied to the tuning year; retrospective policy analysis; departure-time feature not a pre-departure forecast; Study 2 agents selected from Study 1; compute meter excludes model inference; costs are rate-card projections; compliance traces only find anticipated violations. Gaps: pre-specified replication on another model family; test of the cache-failure mechanism; interaction of context management with caching. Recommendations: evaluate pairings, repeat attempts, reject non-compliant runs before ranking, confirm on later data, instrument cache share and compute

Abstract says '584 runs': 116 + 312 + 156 = 584. Study 1 table 'Five complete rows' plus partial rows; Study 1 quality excludes 5 of 108 runs. Interaction joint test reported as 'rejects no interaction (chi2 = 12.3, p = 0.002)'. Cost figures exclude cache discounts and reasoning tokens (Studies 2-3). Data, code and every delivered program released (github.com/earino/identical-runs-different-results). No pre-registration (Table 2 distinguishes planned from exploratory analyses).
